title: Night shift work exposure shapes neurobehavioral and cardiometabolic profiles in female healthcare workers: a cross-sectional study.
reason: The report directly measures and analyses waist circumference, an eligible central-adiposity component. Night-shift status is a workplace exposure. Although many reported cardiometabolic indices are outside the prespecified component set, the waist-circumference result is eligible.
action: Retain, but synthesize only the eligible waist/central-adiposity outcome and keep the study outside the core occupational-stress domain.

title: Effectiveness of a Food Education Program for healthcare workers: a pilot study in a Total Worker Health approach.
reason: The intervention is explicitly dietary and workplace-based. The study measures eligible MetS components including triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, fasting glucose and abdominal circumference. These satisfy the prespecified outcome rule even though the paper also reports BMI, WHR, HbA1c and other non-core outcomes.
action: Retain and extract only eligible MetS-component outcomes for synthesis.

title: Mental stress and the risks of metabolic syndrome and related components in military personnel: CHIEF cohort study.
reason: BSRS-5 measures general mental distress (depression, anxiety, hostility, insomnia and interpersonal sensitivity), not occupational/job stress. The occupational population alone does not make the exposure work-related. Physical activity is treated as a covariate rather than the primary exposure of interest.
action: Move to full-text exclusion under wrong exposure/intervention; retain in audit history as a near-scope occupational study.
